title: Language groups in Eastern Africa
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Use arrows on the regional map for the routes as taught: Bantu from the Congo basin and west-central Africa, Nilotes from the Nile valley in South Sudan, Cushites from Ethiopia. Respect every community.

skills.key_step: The child sorts communities of Eastern Africa into the Bantu, Nilotic and Cushitic groups.

floor.prerequisite: Sorts Kenyan communities into language groups.
floor.question: In which group are the Kikuyu?

representations: community cards from across the region
a map of where groups live
steps: Recall or look up its group.
Check with a Kenyan example of the same group.

misconceptions.ask: Which language group do the Luo belong to?
misconceptions.repair: Say the language families: Bantu, Nilotic, Cushitic, and name two for each.

misconceptions.ask: Which language group do the Somali belong to?
misconceptions.repair: Link Cushitic with the Horn: Somali, Oromo, Afar.

misconceptions.ask: Which sub-group of the Nilotes do the Maasai belong to?
misconceptions.repair: Say Plain Nilotes live on the plains and herd cattle, like the Maasai and the Turkana.

misconceptions.ask: Are all Ugandans in the same language group?
misconceptions.repair: Sort communities from one country into all three groups.

checks.question: In which language group are the Chagga?
In which language group are the Acholi?

skills.key_step: The child gives reasons for migration and the origin and direction of each group.

floor.question: In which group are the Somali?

contexts: Bantu moving east from the Congo basin
Nilotes moving south from the Nile valley

board.do: Draw the region and an arrow from South Sudan southwards.
Add the other two arrows and one reason each.

misconceptions.ask: Why did many groups move to new lands?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what a herder does when the grass is gone.

misconceptions.ask: Where did the Bantu come from?
misconceptions.repair: Match each group with its homeland in a three-row table.

misconceptions.ask: Which way did the Cushites move into Kenya?
misconceptions.repair: Find Ethiopia and Kenya on a map and say which is north.

misconceptions.ask: Did the Bantu reach Eastern Africa in one journey?
misconceptions.repair: Draw the arrow in short steps with dates beside them.

checks.question: Where did the Cushites come from?
checks.answer: Ethiopia and the Horn of Africa

checks.question: Give two reasons for migration.
checks.answer: any two of: pasture and water, fertile land, drought, famine, disease, wars, overcrowding, trade

skills.key_step: The child gives effects of migration and settlement, good and bad.
representations: a story of two communities meeting
steps: Ask what changed for the people already there.

board.do: Draw a T-chart: good and bad.

board.say: What did communities gain when they met?

misconceptions.repair: Ask what happens when two herds need the same water.

misconceptions.ask: What happened when groups settled near each other?
misconceptions.repair: Ask whether Kikuyu and Maasai speak the same language today.

misconceptions.ask: Give one good effect of migration.
misconceptions.repair: Draw a T-chart and fill the good side first.

misconceptions.ask: Which skill did the Bantu spread as they migrated?
misconceptions.repair: Show a picture of a traditional smelting furnace.

checks.question: Give one good effect of migration.
checks.answer: any of: intermarriage, mixing of cultures, trade, spread of farming and iron working

checks.question: Give one bad effect of migration.
checks.answer: any of: conflict over land, displacement, disease spread
